name: m1_crosslayer_feature
stressor: cross-layer feature threading: one new required datum (tenant_id) must reach AND be USED at every layer; omitting it at any single layer breaks behavior
source_note: Purpose-built 'ledger' package (10 Python modules) modeling a Controller -> Service -> Repository -> Store stack with a Serializer. Grounded in the canonical multi-tenant request-scoping pattern: a required tenant_id must be threaded through every layer of a layered app and USED at each (scope repository reads/writes, enforce ownership in the service, read it off the request in the controller, stamp it into the serialized response). Real-world references: django-multitenant requires a tenant_id on every TenantModel and scopes all ORM queries by it (https://github.com/citusdata/django-multitenant -- 'Define a static variable named tenant_id and specify the tenant column'; Model.save() injects tenant_id), and the FastAPI/asgi-correlation-id pattern threads a per-request id through middleware -> service -> repository -> response header (https://github.com/snok/asgi-correlation-id). auth.py is a distractor: it has its own unrelated local variable also named tenant_id (a parsed token field) that must NOT be rewired; version.py is a second distractor.
discriminator: The new required datum tenant_id must be threaded through and genuinely USED at 4 interdependent layers at once -- repository.get/list/create/save must filter & stamp by tenant, service.open_account/get_account/list_accounts/deposit must accept & forward it and enforce ownership (cross-tenant -> NotFoundError), controller.handle must read request['tenant_id'] and pass it down, and serializer must emit the tenant under 'tenant' -- while auth.py's same-named local tenant_id must stay byte-identical. A bounded-slice agent keeps every layer in its working set and threads the field consistently top-to-bottom; a growing-transcript agent must repeatedly re-derive the call chain and tends to drop the datum at one layer (e.g. fixes service+controller but forgets repository scoping so cross-tenant rows still leak, or forgets the serializer 'tenant' key, or blanket-edits the auth.py distractor).
